questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I just listed cities I had been in before and that I liked.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked the experience, and I would recommend it!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: University of Iceland were very helpful and provided all needed information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We could just go to the Service desk at all times and they knew everything I needed to know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The mentor system was very nice to have, and everybody really helped a lot.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student Housing - it wasent directly on campus, but maybe 200 meters from the University

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I shared a kitchen with 9 other people, and I could just use it as much as I wanted.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Sign up in good time!! If you sign up like 6 months before, you will definitly get housing in student housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was quite expensive, which was the only downside.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just applied for the courses, that KU has approved me to take, and I got a spot at them all.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could email them and they always answered quite fast - that was great.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got a spot in all I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do it in good time, then there shouldnt be any problems.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 4 BA courses and one MA

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were no long lectures at University of Iceland, it was all in class with 1 professor and max. 50 students. It was inclusive, discussing the topics were encouraged.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: All that glitters is not gold, Small State Theory, Arctic Politics in international context, Hybrid Threats, Leadership in Small States

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course on Hybrid Threats were very interesting, and nothing we have learned about in Copenhagen!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything was just more expensive than I had thought - a beer at a bar costs around 100 DKK for instance, and food is also really expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alchohol and food were more expensive than I thought - nothing was cheaper than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didnt really use any of them - except the student cellar. It is very nice to have a place for studing, hanging out, that has nothing to do with school.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of people used the University gym - it was very cheap. We also had orientation week, and the Student Cellar was always open - a bar, where you can also order food and just sit and study.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Reykjavik is a very small city, so I recommoned going out of the city - rent a car even just for a day adn go to the high lands - it is very beautiful.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips in the summer! After october, the weather becomes really bad, so go while you can - visit Akyreyri, the south and Laumannerlauger!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - it is a lot like the Danish one, except you have to participate more in class. That was difficult at first, but ended up being great.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didnt really get any local friends, so I wouldnt know

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any - Icelandic culture is a lot like the Danish, and many people even speak Danish.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It was very nice to live in such an open environment - there is not much racism or homophobia in Iceland, which I really appriciated.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Check if you can get the courses approved by KU beforehand, Sign up for Student Housing early and sign up for a mentor! It is a great help

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was almost impossible for me to get my courses approved from University of Copenhagen, since University of Iceland dosent have too many courses to choose from. So check before hand if it is possible to get the courses, that you need!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many nice people - and the feeling of building a new life in a new place (and succiding in it) was very rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Funding it - Iceland is a very expensive country, and the Student Housing is also expensive. I didnt get any scholarships, so I had to work in Iceland to fund it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: My recommendation would be to get a job! I got a lot of great friends there and I had something to do on the days where we didnt have school (plus Iceland is expensive, so it aint bad to have a salary)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
